title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
excerpt: [astro-ph.EP] We present 14 optical imaging and eight optical spectroscopic epochs of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Keck/LRIS and Gemini/GMOS, two near-infrared (NIR) imaging epochs from Keck/MOSFIRE, and four NIR spectroscopic […]
content:
[astro-ph.EP] We present 14 optical imaging and eight optical spectroscopic epochs of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Keck/LRIS and Gemini/GMOS, two near-infrared (NIR) imaging epochs from Keck/MOSFIRE, and four NIR spectroscopic epochs from Gemini/Flamingos-2 and GNIRS, obtained between 2025 July and 2026 May.

Mean GMOS colors of g−r=0.732±0.029, r−i=0.237±0.025, and i−z=0.109±0.022 mag show no significant change across perihelion. Phase-corrected red-band activity follows Afρ∝r−2.10±0.14h inbound and r−3.34±0.43h outbound. Transverse-width and sunward-plume speeds imply dust losses of 2.7×109 and 1.0×1010 kg over 2025 July 3–2026 May 15 for 1-μm–1-mm grains, equivalent to global layers of 0.26 and 0.99 m under the adopted grain and nucleus assumptions.

The concentrated coma, compact sunward feature, and antisolar tail seen on 2025 August 27 broadened by 2025 November 26; extended dust persisted through 2026 February 17. C2/CN nearly doubled from 0.257±0.014 on 2025 September 14–15 to 0.481±0.080 on 2025 November 26, while C3/CN fell from 0.327±0.024 on 2025 August 28 to 0.214±0.009 on 2025 September 14–15.

MOSFIRE NIR imaging on 2025 July 11 gives Y−J=0.466±0.143, J−H=0.239±0.052, H−Ks=0.454±0.150, and J−Ks=0.693±0.202 mag. Spectra give J−H=0.24 mag on 2025 September 5–6 and J−H=0.27–0.28 and J−Ks=0.21–0.22 mag on 2025 December 1–2 over the retained passband intervals.

Model-calibrated imaging on 2026 February 6 gives near-solar J−Ks=0.303±0.051 mag. No water-ice absorption is robust to the tested continuum and calibration choices in the NIR spectra. These observations provide a lasting record of the comet’s evolution through the Solar System and a benchmark for studying and monitoring future interstellar objects.
